newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady as offshore parties ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady as offshore parties ruled out.

text.p: The fragile Thai baht stabilised in late quiet trade on Friday after the Bank of Thailand asked local banks to stop quoting transactions with offshore players, dealers said.
The baht was trading at 25.775/25.875 to the dollar late against 25.450/25.650 in early morning, dealers said. The mid-rate was fixed at 25.82 to the dollar compared with 25.81 on Thursday.
"The market was almost silent today as we did not have transactions with offshore players," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

The Bank of Thailand on Friday made it clear that foreign speculators who sold the baht heavily for U.S. dollars would have to pay a high price for their action by buying back baht from the more expensive swap market to square outstanding positions.

"We separate local investors from outside speculators in terms of liquidity supply. The outside speculators cannot buy baht back to meet obligations through regular channels. For Thai business, everything will be normal," said Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi.
Dealers said the exemption of offshore parties from dollar selling was expected to continue until Monday as the central bank wanted to make sure that the market really normalised.
"We did only transactions for our corporate clients. I think the central bank's measure will still exist on Monday," said another dealer.
The one-month swap premium was down sharply to 30/55 satangs per dollar late from as high as 70/100 in the morning.
"Offshore players were trading among themselves today. The swap premiums fell sharply in the afternoon as the situation seemed to calm down," said another dealer.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 15.00-18.00 percent in late trade from 20.00-22.00 in early morning on steadily rising liquidity, dealers said.
